transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Yeah, um... well, I came in because I went from barely settling into my new apartment—which, by the way, has this amazing natural light. I spent months looking for a south-facing place because my monsteras were literally dying in my old place, and plant care is just so expensive now with the special soils and everything. You wouldn't believe how much a bag of perlite costs these days. 

But anyway, yeah, I went from just trying to unpack to suddenly saying yes to all these mentoring sessions. And I started taking on extra client prototypes, too. Which is a lot, because as a digital designer, clients always want everything yesterday and they never actually know what they want until you build it. And then I was redesigning my whole portfolio on top of all that. It just felt like I had to fix my entire life in one sprint. So... yeah, I guess that's why I made the appointment.
Have you been feeling unusually happy or energetic lately?

Yeah, um, I guess energetic is one way to put it. Earlier this month, I felt almost... electric, you know? Like really upbeat and just buzzing. But then, it's weird, because one minute I'm on top of the world, and the next I'm just snapping at people. I totally went off on this freelance contractor I work with, and then my sister, just over these tiny delays. It felt like they were personally trying to block me from getting things done. 

Which is so frustrating because my sister is usually the one who gets it. She's a teacher, so she deals with delays all the time, especially with the new curriculum they rolled out this year. Have you heard about that? They changed the math standards again, and she spends her entire weekend just trying to figure out how to teach fractions to second graders. I tried to help her design some visual aids for it, but honestly, second graders are tough critics. They just want bright colors and dinosaurs. I actually thought about doing a whole series of educational apps with dinosaurs, but then I'd have to learn Swift, and Apple's developer guidelines are just a nightmare to navigate... Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, energetic. Yeah, definitely buzzing, but also really irritable.
Have you experienced any periods of feeling sad or empty in the past few weeks?

Yeah, um... actually, yes. It's been really hard. Lately I wake up with this... this heavy, gray feeling right in my chest. And it doesn't even make sense because the apartment will be totally quiet, nothing bad is happening at all, but I just feel so drained. Like, I'll walk into the kitchen and see a single coffee mug sitting in the sink, and I feel like I could just break down and cry over it. 

Which is ridiculous because it's just a mug. It's actually this really beautiful handmade ceramic one I got at an art fair a couple of years ago. The glaze on it is this gorgeous speckled teal, and the artist was telling me how she fires them in this special kiln that makes every single pattern unique. I always meant to take a pottery class, actually. Working with clay seems so therapeutic, you know? Just getting your hands dirty and not looking at a screen. Because my eyes get so strained from staring at Figma all day. I bought those blue-light blocking glasses they advertise everywhere on Instagram, but I swear they just give everything this weird yellow tint that totally messes up my color palettes when I'm designing, so I can't even wear them for work... wait. Sorry. What was I saying? Oh, feeling sad. Right. Yeah, just waking up with that heavy gray feeling and wanting to cry over dishes.
Have you experienced any periods where you didn't need much sleep?

Yeah, definitely. Um, for a few nights there, I was sleeping maybe three or four hours tops. But the weird thing was, I'd wake up feeling totally fine. Like, completely rested and just convinced I should use the extra hours to get ahead on things. 

Which is normally impossible for me because I love my sleep. I actually just invested in this amazing memory foam mattress topper. It was supposed to be cooling, you know, because my new apartment gets so warm with all that natural light I mentioned. But honestly, I think the cooling gel is a scam. It just feels like regular foam to me. I spent hours reading reviews on Reddit before I bought it, too. There's this whole community of people who are obsessed with sleep optimization. They talk about sleep hygiene and circadian rhythms and tracking your REM cycles with those smart rings. I thought about getting one of those rings, but they're so chunky, and I type all day, so I feel like it would just clack against the keyboard and drive me crazy. Plus, they come in such limited metal finishes. As a designer, I just can't wear something that clashes with my everyday jewelry. Like, if I'm wearing gold, I can't have a titanium ring on, it just ruins the whole aesthetic... um, wait, sorry. Sleep. Yeah, I was barely sleeping at all, just a few hours, but I felt totally ready to go.
Do you feel like your irritability and sadness are connected to your high-energy periods, or do they seem to happen independently of each other?

Um, I think they kind of happen on their own? Like, the irritability definitely spikes when I'm feeling super energetic and buzzing, but the sadness... that's been its own thing. The heavier depressive stretches have actually been showing up since my separation about 11 months ago. That was even before this latest move made everything sharper and more intense. 

Which, honestly, moving is just the worst process ever. I don't know how people do it regularly. I had to hire these movers who promised they were experts in handling delicate furniture, and they still managed to scratch my mid-century modern credenza. It's a vintage piece I found at this amazing estate sale up in the Hudson Valley. The woman running the sale was telling me how her grandparents brought it over from Denmark in the 60s. I love estate sales, you can find such incredible history in people's homes. I went to one last summer where they had this massive collection of vintage Pyrex bowls, the really colorful ones? People go absolutely crazy for those online. There are whole Facebook groups dedicated to just trading Pyrex patterns. I thought about buying them to resell, but honestly, shipping glass just seems like a logistical nightmare with all the bubble wrap you'd need, and bubble wrap isn't very eco-friendly anyway. I try to use that corrugated cardboard stuff when I ship things, but it just doesn't protect the corners as well... wait, what were you asking? Oh, if they're connected. Yeah, the sadness has been around for about 11 months, since the separation, kind of doing its own thing.
When you're feeling really energetic and buzzing, does it feel like you're in a completely different state from your normal self?

Yeah, um, it definitely feels like a totally different state. Like, earlier this month, I felt almost... electric, you know? Just completely upbeat and buzzing one minute, but then I'd just snap. Like, I snapped at this contractor who was supposed to be fixing a leak, and then at my sister, over these tiny, stupid delays. It felt like they were personally trying to block me from getting things done. 

Which is so frustrating because dealing with contractors is already a nightmare. You hire them, they say they'll be there between 8 AM and noon, and then they show up at 3 PM like it's totally fine. And I'm just sitting there, trying to work on this massive redesign project for a client. They wanted a complete overhaul of their e-commerce site, but their brand guidelines are so outdated. They're still using this awful drop-shadow effect on all their buttons that looks straight out of 2010. I tried explaining to them that flat design or neumorphism is way more current, but they just wouldn't listen. It's like talking to a brick wall. People get so attached to their terrible logos, too. I had a client once who insisted on keeping this pixelated mascot from when they founded the company in the 90s, and no matter how much I tried to modernize it, they kept saying it lost its "charm." Charm? It looks like a glitch! I don't know why people hire designers if they aren't going to trust their expertise, you know? It just makes the whole process take twice as long, and then they wonder why the billable hours are so high... oh, sorry. I got off track again. But yeah, when I get in that buzzing state, it's like I'm electric and upbeat, but then I get so irritable and snap at people over the smallest things.
How long do these periods of feeling electric and buzzing usually last?

Um, well, this whole intense up-and-down pattern, the buzzing and then the snapping, it's really been going on since I moved into the new apartment about a month ago. 

Which, by the way, I still haven't fully unpacked because I keep getting distracted by how the lighting hits the walls in the afternoon. It's this really harsh, direct light, and I've been trying to find the perfect sheer curtains to diffuse it. I went to this fabric district downtown last week, and it was just overwhelming. There are literally thousands of bolts of fabric, and the salespeople are so aggressive. They just follow you around with these giant scissors, waiting for you to point at something. I ended up buying this linen blend that was way over my budget, but it has this gorgeous, organic texture. Linen is so tricky though, isn't it? Like, you look at it and it wrinkles. I have this linen blazer I bought for client meetings, and I have to steam it for twenty minutes before I can even walk out the door. I bought one of those handheld steamers, the ones they use on fashion shoots? But it spits water everywhere. I ruined a silk blouse last month because the steamer just burped boiling water right onto the collar. Silk is impossible to clean, too. You take it to the dry cleaner, and they charge you like twenty dollars for one shirt, and half the time it comes back smelling like chemicals anyway... wait. Sorry. How long does it last. Yeah, this whole buzzing thing has been happening for about a month, basically since the move.
When you're feeling electric and buzzing, do you usually come back down to a normal state before feeling that way again?

Um, do I come back to normal? I'm not really sure if I hit a baseline normal in between, to be honest. It's kind of hard to gauge what normal even is lately, especially with trying to set up a normal routine in the new place. 

Like, I tried to establish this perfect morning routine to ground myself, you know? I bought this incredibly expensive burr grinder for my coffee beans because I read that the standard blade grinders just smash the beans and completely ruin the flavor profile. And I'm really particular about my coffee. I only buy light roast Ethiopian beans from this local roaster down the street. The guy who runs it is so pretentious, though. He literally refused to sell my friend a bag of dark roast once because he said it "insults the bean." Can you believe that? It's just bean juice! But anyway, the burr grinder I got is so loud, it sounds like a jet engine taking off in my kitchen, which is not exactly the peaceful morning vibe I was going for. I've been looking into manual hand grinders instead, the ones with the ceramic burrs? But they take like five minutes of aggressive cranking just to get enough grounds for one pour-over, and my wrists already ache from using the mouse all day for design work. Ergonomic mice are so ugly, by the way. They look like weird alien spaceships. I tried one that was essentially a vertical joystick, and it took me a week just to figure out how to click and drag properly without my hand cramping up... 

Wait, what did you ask? Oh, right, coming back down to normal. Yeah, I honestly don't know if I fully come back down or not. It all just kind of blurs together right now.
Do you feel like you're switching between these high-energy states and your more normal or low-energy states, or is it more of a continuous fluctuation?

Um, continuous fluctuation? I don't know... maybe? I really haven't been keeping track of the switches, to be honest. It's just hard to tell when one thing ends and another begins. 

Kind of like how my lease started on the first, but I didn't actually get the keys until the third because the property manager went on vacation. Which is just wild to me. Who goes on vacation at the beginning of the month when rent is due and people are moving in? He went to Cabo, too, because I saw his out-of-office email. I've always wanted to go to Cabo, but the flights are just ridiculously expensive right now. I was looking at flights to Mexico last night instead of sleeping, actually, because I got this targeted ad for a boutique hotel in Tulum that has these incredible hanging macrame chairs in the lobby. I spent like three hours trying to source the exact same chairs for a client's patio redesign, but the shipping costs from the artisans in Mexico were astronomical. And then you have to deal with customs, which is a total nightmare. I ordered this vintage rug from Morocco once, and it sat in customs for six weeks. When it finally arrived, it smelled like wet dog and mothballs. I had to pay a professional cleaner more than the rug cost just to get the smell out, and even now, if it gets humid in the apartment, you can still catch a whiff of it. It's so frustrating because it ties the whole room together perfectly, the colors are just so vibrant... 

Wait, sorry. Switching states? Yeah, I really don't know if it's switching or just continuous. I haven't noticed a clear pattern.
Do you feel like you're having distinct episodes of feeling electric and buzzing, or is it more of a general mood that you're in lately?

Um, distinct episodes? Well, earlier this month, yeah, it was definitely distinct. I felt almost electric and upbeat one minute, like totally dialed in, and then the next minute I just snapped. Like, I snapped at this contractor we use for work, and then my sister, over these tiny, stupid delays. It felt like they were personally trying to block me from getting things done, you know? 

Which is ridiculous because my sister is usually the reliable one. She actually just had a baby, my new niece, and she's been so stressed about getting the nursery finished. I offered to help her paint it because she picked this awful, sterile hospital green color, and I was like, "No, we need something warmer, like a soft sage or a muted terracotta." But she wouldn't listen. She's so stubborn. We went to the hardware store to look at swatches, and the guy working in the paint department was completely useless. He didn't even know the difference between an eggshell and a satin finish. How do you work in a paint department and not know that? It's literally the most basic thing. I ended up just grabbing a bunch of samples and mixing them myself on a piece of cardboard in her driveway. Which, by the way, is a terrible idea because driveway asphalt completely throws off your perception of the undertones. The gray of the street makes everything look too yellow... 

Oh, wait. What were we talking about? The episodes, right. Yeah, earlier this month it was definitely like, electric and then snapping at people.
Do you feel like these episodes of feeling electric and buzzing keep happening over time, or was it just a one-time thing?

Um, keeps happening? Yeah, it's definitely not just a one-time thing. This whole intense up-and-down pattern has basically been going on since I moved into the new apartment about a month ago. 

Which, by the way, I still have like twenty boxes sitting in my living room that I haven't unpacked. I bought these really specific, minimalist acrylic storage bins to organize all my design materials, because visual clutter just completely ruins my workflow. But the bins ended up being slightly too tall for the shelving unit I ordered. And don't even get me started on that delivery. The guy literally left the flat packs out in the hallway instead of bringing them inside, and my neighbor actually complained to the building manager about them blocking the walkway. She's this older woman who has this tiny, aggressive Pomeranian that barks at literally the air. I swear that dog is a menace. I tried giving it a dog treat once when we were waiting for the elevator, just to make peace, but she looked at me like I was trying to poison her precious baby. People are so incredibly weird about their pets in this building. Like, they have a dedicated dog spa on the first floor, but the human gym equipment is from like 2010. The treadmill belt slips every time you step on it, which is so dangerous... 

Wait, sorry, I lost my train of thought again. The episodes? Yeah, it's been an ongoing thing for about a month now, ever since the move.
Do you usually feel depressed or really down after one of these episodes where you feel electric and buzzing?

Um, depressed? Yeah, I definitely get these really low crashes. Lately I'll wake up with this heavy, gray feeling in my chest. Even when the apartment is totally quiet and nothing bad is actually happening, I feel like I could just break down and cry over a coffee mug left in the sink. 

Which is so stupid, because I'm the one who left the mug there. It's this beautiful handmade ceramic one I got at a craft fair in Brooklyn last year. The glaze has this incredible speckled texture, kind of like a robin's egg but deeper. The artist actually told me she mixes her own glazes using local materials, which I think is so authentic. I tried taking a pottery class once to see if I could make my own stuff, but the wheel is so much harder to control than it looks. You have to keep your elbows locked into your sides, and my core strength is just shot right now because I haven't been doing my Pilates. I signed up for this online Pilates subscription, thinking I'd do it in the living room, but like I said, the boxes are everywhere. Plus, the instructor in the videos has this really grating, overly enthusiastic voice. Like, nobody is that happy about doing a hundred crunches at 7 AM, Jessica. It's just fake. I prefer the instructors who actually acknowledge that it burns. I used to go to this studio downtown where the instructor would play vintage disco music, and it was such a vibe. The lighting was always this moody amber color...

Wait, sorry. The crashing feeling? Yeah, that heavy, gray feeling in my chest has been happening a lot lately. I just feel so down for no reason.
Do you typically feel completely normal and fine between these episodes of feeling electric and buzzing?

Um, normal in between? Not really, no. Honestly, the heavier depressive stretches have been showing up since my separation about 11 months ago. Even before this latest move made everything sharper, I was having these long periods of just feeling totally drained. 

Which, the separation was a whole nightmare of its own. We had to divide up all the furniture, and he actually tried to claim the mid-century modern credenza that I found at an estate sale. I spent three weeks restoring the teak wood on that thing. You have to use a very specific oil, not that cheap hardware store stuff, or it completely ruins the grain. And he didn't even care about the aesthetic! He just wanted it to put his massive, ugly television on. He always had terrible taste in electronics. He bought this sound system that had wires running everywhere, completely ruining the visual flow of the living room. I tried getting him to buy cable concealers, the ones that you paint to match the wall, but he said it was "too much effort." It's literally just peeling a sticky back and pressing it to the baseboard. But that was him in a nutshell, you know? Always taking the easy way out. He couldn't even be bothered to load the dishwasher correctly. He'd put the bowls facing up so they'd just fill with dirty water. I mean, who does that? It defies basic physics. 

Oh, right, sorry. Normal between the electric feelings? No, the depressive stretches have been pretty consistent for almost a year now, since the separation.
Do you feel like you return to your completely normal self between these episodes of feeling electric and buzzing?

Um, wait, didn't you just ask me that? Like, if I feel normal in between the buzzing times? I thought I just said... no, not really. Because of the heavy, drained feeling that's been going on since the separation. 

Which is why I haven't even been able to focus on my freelance projects. I had this one client last week who wanted me to redesign their entire e-commerce checkout flow, and they wanted it done in three days. Three days! And their current site is a disaster. They're using this awful neon green for their primary call-to-action buttons, which completely clashes with their brand identity, and the font is some generic sans-serif that looks like it's from 2005. I tried explaining to them that color psychology is crucial for conversion rates, especially in the wellness sector, but they were so stubborn about keeping the green because the CEO's daughter picked it out. I mean, why hire a professional designer if you're just going to let a teenager make the creative decisions? It's like going to a Michelin-star restaurant and asking for ketchup. I actually did that once, well, not ketchup, but I asked for hot sauce at this really fancy French place because the bisque was just so bland. The waiter looked at me like I had just insulted his ancestors. It was so uncomfortable. But honestly, if you're going to charge forty dollars for soup, it should have some flavor...

Anyway, yeah, sorry. Like I just said, no, I don't really go back to normal. The low, drained stretches have been happening for almost a year now.
Do you feel like you're clearly switching in and out of these electric and buzzing states, or is it more of a gradual shift?

Um, switching in and out? I don't know, I haven't really noticed if it's like a clear switch or gradual. I guess I just haven't paid that much attention to the exact moment it changes. 

I was actually trying to track my moods with this app I downloaded, but the interface was so clunky. It had these horrible drop-down menus that took forever to load, and the color scheme was this really aggressive orange and purple combo. It's like the developers didn't even consult a UX designer before launching it. And they kept sending me these push notifications at the most random times, like 3 PM on a Tuesday, asking "How are you feeling right now?" Like, I'm working, obviously! Well, trying to work. I actually missed a deadline on Tuesday because my internet kept dropping out. My ISP is an absolute joke. I've called them three times this week, and every time I get put on hold for forty-five minutes, listening to this incredibly compressed, tinny elevator music. It's always that same royalty-free jazz loop. I don't understand why companies can't invest in better hold music. There's this one indie radio station I listen to that plays the most amazing ambient electronic tracks, and it's so soothing. I tried to find the playlist on Spotify, but the algorithm just keeps recommending me generic lo-fi beats to study to, which is not the same thing at all. The compression on those tracks completely flattens the bass...

Wait, what was the question? Oh, if it's a clear switch or gradual. Yeah, I really couldn't tell you. I haven't noticed how it happens.
Do you feel like these episodes of feeling electric and buzzing are separate events, or is it more of a constant fluctuation?

Um, I guess it feels more like a fluctuation? Because, like, earlier this month, I'd feel almost electric and completely upbeat one minute, and then the next I'd just snap. I totally snapped at this freelance contractor, and then my sister, over these tiny little delays. It just felt like they were personally trying to block me from getting things done, you know? 

Especially the contractor. I hired him to handle some back-end database stuff for a project because I strictly do digital interface design, and he swore he knew how to integrate this custom booking widget. Well, two days go by, and he tells me the documentation is "confusing." Confusing? It's literally the most well-documented API on the internet. A middle schooler could figure it out. If you call yourself a full-stack developer, you should know how to read basic documentation. 

And don't even get me started on my sister. She was supposed to drop off my spare apartment keys, and she was an hour late because she stopped to get an iced matcha latte. Do you have any idea how much sugar is in those cafe matchas? It's basically a green milkshake masquerading as a health drink. I tried to explain to her that she's just spiking her glycemic index and setting herself up for a massive afternoon crash, but she never listens to me. She buys all these "wellness" gummies she sees on TikTok that are just overpriced gelatin and food coloring. The packaging on them is always so manipulative, too—using these soft, earthy pastel tones to imply they're organic when the second ingredient is corn syrup...

Wait, sorry. Did I answer the question? You were asking if it fluctuates or if they are separate. Yeah, it definitely fluctuates really fast. Upbeat and buzzing one second, and then I'm biting someone's head off the next.
Do you feel like you're a completely different person when you're in one of these electric and buzzing states?

Um, a completely different person? I don't know if I'd say a completely different person... I mean, I'm still me, just... faster? Louder? I don't really know how to describe it. It's not like I wake up and I'm suddenly someone else entirely. 

Though, honestly, sometimes I wish I was someone else. Like, someone who doesn't have to deal with freelance taxes. Have you ever tried to navigate the quarterly estimated tax portal? It is a nightmare. The user interface looks like it was built in 1998 and never updated. The text is so small, and there's absolutely no visual hierarchy. It's just blocks and blocks of gray text on a gray background. It's incredibly hostile to the user. I actually wrote a very polite email to the IRS webmaster—if they even have one—suggesting some basic accessibility improvements, like increasing the contrast ratio and maybe using a sans-serif font that doesn't make your eyes bleed. I even offered to do a free consultation, just because it bothered me so much. But of course, I never heard back. Government agencies are just a black hole for good design. It's like they actively want you to be miserable while giving them your money. My accountant told me to just use this third-party software instead, but that software has this really annoying animated paperclip mascot that pops up every five seconds. It's so distracting when I'm trying to categorize my business expenses...

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, being a different person. Yeah, I don't think so. I'm not sure, I've never really thought of it like being a totally different person.
Do you feel like you're having distinct episodes of feeling electric and buzzing, or is it more of a general mood that you're in lately?

Um, distinct episodes or a general mood? I guess... well, this whole intense up-and-down pattern, the buzzing and then the snapping, it's been going on since I moved into my new apartment about a month ago. 

Which, by the way, moving is the absolute worst. The property management company completely lied about the natural light in the living room. They used these wide-angle lenses and bumped up the exposure in the listing photos to make it look bright and airy, but it actually faces a brick wall. It's so deceptive. I've been trying to compensate by buying all these smart bulbs so I can program the color temperature to mimic daylight, but the app that controls them is a disaster. It drops the Bluetooth connection constantly. I spent three hours last night just trying to sync the hallway lights so they fade up gradually in the morning. The user manual was just a single piece of paper with a QR code that linked to a broken 404 page. It's honestly shocking how these companies stay in business with such terrible quality control. I ended up having to dig through a Reddit thread from three years ago just to find a workaround for the firmware update. And don't even get me started on the people in that subreddit—they were so incredibly condescending when someone asked a basic question about the API bridge...

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? You were asking about the episodes. But yeah, it's basically been this general up-and-down thing for the last month since the move.
Do you feel like your electric and buzzing states have lasted for at least one week?

Well, yeah, like I think I just mentioned a second ago, it's definitely been more than a week. This whole intense up-and-down pattern, the buzzing and everything, has been going on since I moved into the apartment, which was about a month ago. 

And honestly, I still haven't even fully unpacked because I've been trying to find a decent ergonomic office chair. Since I'm at my desk doing interface design for like ten hours a day, I need proper lumbar support, right? You'd think buying a chair would be easy, but every single one online has these obviously fake five-star reviews. They clearly use bots to upvote these generic comments like "Very good sitting!" It's infuriating. I ended up ordering this minimalist Scandinavian one that cost way too much, and it arrived in like fifty pieces with a cheap little Allen wrench that stripped the screws on the very first turn. Why do they even include those? It's honestly an insult to basic engineering. I had to go all the way down to the hardware store to get a proper set of tools, and the guy working there didn't even know the difference between metric and imperial hex keys. I had to literally show him how his own inventory was organized on the shelf... 

Wait, sorry. Did I lose track again? You were asking if it's been a week. Yes. More than a week. A whole month of this pattern.
Have your electric and buzzing states lasted for at least four consecutive days?

Wait, didn't we just... I mean, yes? Four days, a week, it's all wrapped up in the same thing. Like I was just saying a second ago, this whole intense up-and-down pattern has been going on for a solid month, ever since the apartment move. So definitely more than four consecutive days. 

It actually kind of reminds me of this awful checkout flow I was auditing last week. You know when you check a box that says "billing address same as shipping address," but the site forces you to manually type the whole thing out again anyway? It's a classic friction point. I wrote this whole case study on how redundant form fields increase cart abandonment by like, forty percent. People just don't have the patience to repeat themselves to a machine. And the worst part is, the error states on this particular form didn't even highlight which field was missing! It just threw a generic red text box at the top of the page saying "An error occurred." Like, okay, thank you for nothing! How is the user supposed to know they forgot to select their state from a dropdown menu that isn't even alphabetized properly? They had "Wyoming" right between "Wisconsin" and "West Virginia." It's just lazy database management, and it makes me want to pull my hair out when developers don't think about the end user's cognitive load... 

But, um... yeah. Four days. Yes. Like I said, it's been a whole month.

patient.answer:
Um, distinct episodes or a general mood? I guess... well, this whole intense up-and-down pattern, the buzzing and then the snapping, it's been going on since I moved into my new apartment about a month ago. 

Which, by the way, moving is the absolute worst. The property management company completely lied about the natural light in the living room. They used these wide-angle lenses and bumped up the exposure in the listing photos to make it look bright and airy, but it actually faces a brick wall. It's so deceptive. I've been trying to compensate by buying all these smart bulbs so I can program the color temperature to mimic daylight, but the app that controls them is a disaster. It drops the Bluetooth connection constantly. I spent three hours last night just trying to sync the hallway lights so they fade up gradually in the morning. The user manual was just a single piece of paper with a QR code that linked to a broken 404 page. It's honestly shocking how these companies stay in business with such terrible quality control. I ended up having to dig through a Reddit thread from three years ago just to find a workaround for the firmware update. And don't even get me started on the people in that subreddit—they were so incredibly condescending when someone asked a basic question about the API bridge...

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? You were asking about the episodes. But yeah, it's basically been this general up-and-down thing for the last month since the move.

patient.answer:
Well, yeah, like I think I just mentioned a second ago, it's definitely been more than a week. This whole intense up-and-down pattern, the buzzing and everything, has been going on since I moved into the apartment, which was about a month ago. 

And honestly, I still haven't even fully unpacked because I've been trying to find a decent ergonomic office chair. Since I'm at my desk doing interface design for like ten hours a day, I need proper lumbar support, right? You'd think buying a chair would be easy, but every single one online has these obviously fake five-star reviews. They clearly use bots to upvote these generic comments like "Very good sitting!" It's infuriating. I ended up ordering this minimalist Scandinavian one that cost way too much, and it arrived in like fifty pieces with a cheap little Allen wrench that stripped the screws on the very first turn. Why do they even include those? It's honestly an insult to basic engineering. I had to go all the way down to the hardware store to get a proper set of tools, and the guy working there didn't even know the difference between metric and imperial hex keys. I had to literally show him how his own inventory was organized on the shelf... 

Wait, sorry. Did I lose track again? You were asking if it's been a week. Yes. More than a week. A whole month of this pattern.

doctor.question: Have your electric and buzzing states lasted for at least four consecutive days?

patient.answer:
Wait, didn't we just... I mean, yes? Four days, a week, it's all wrapped up in the same thing. Like I was just saying a second ago, this whole intense up-and-down pattern has been going on for a solid month, ever since the apartment move. So definitely more than four consecutive days. 

It actually kind of reminds me of this awful checkout flow I was auditing last week. You know when you check a box that says "billing address same as shipping address," but the site forces you to manually type the whole thing out again anyway? It's a classic friction point. I wrote this whole case study on how redundant form fields increase cart abandonment by like, forty percent. People just don't have the patience to repeat themselves to a machine. And the worst part is, the error states on this particular form didn't even highlight which field was missing! It just threw a generic red text box at the top of the page saying "An error occurred." Like, okay, thank you for nothing! How is the user supposed to know they forgot to select their state from a dropdown menu that isn't even alphabetized properly? They had "Wyoming" right between "Wisconsin" and "West Virginia." It's just lazy database management, and it makes me want to pull my hair out when developers don't think about the end user's cognitive load... 

But, um... yeah. Four days. Yes. Like I said, it's been a whole month.
